I added open and close transitions to all three in CSS only, in `src/styles.css`. `app.js` still toggles `hidden` and `.is-open` as before. I haven't run it in a browser, so none of the motion has been checked on screen.

**How it works:** each element now stays on screen while its exit plays, and starts from a hidden state when it opens, so it animates both ways instead of just appearing and disappearing. If you reopen something while it's closing, it reverses smoothly from where it is. Everything uses your existing motion tokens: opening takes `--duration-medium` (250ms), closing takes `--duration-short` (150ms), and both use `--ease-standard`.

- **Account dropdown:** fades in and grows from 0.96 to full size, starting from its top-right corner, under the button it's aligned to.
- **"Changes saved" toast:** fades in and rises 16px from the bottom of the screen, then drops back down as it fades out.
- **Delete-account modal:** the dark backdrop fades in while the card grows from 0.96 at its centre. The modal's broken `transition: all 400ms ease` is gone. Because the modal switched from `display: none`, that transition never had anything to animate from.

**Reduced motion:** for users who turn on "reduce motion", all three only fade. No growing or sliding.

**Browser support:** this needs Chrome 117+, Safari 17.4+ or Firefox 129+. Older browsers show and hide the elements instantly, as they do now.

**Other issues I saw but didn't fix**, since they're outside this request:
- The delete modal doesn't move keyboard focus into itself, keep focus inside while open, or close on Escape.
- The `.menu a:hover` style isn't limited to devices that can hover. On touch screens the highlight stays stuck after a tap.

I added open and close transitions to all three overlays. The changes are only in `src/styles.css`; `app.js` still just toggles `hidden` and `.is-open`. I haven't tested this in a browser, so the motion still needs a look.

**How each one moves**
- **Account dropdown:** fades and grows from 0.96 to full size, starting from its top-right corner (where the menu sits under the button).
- **"Changes saved" toast:** fades in while rising 16px from the bottom of the screen, and drops back down when it closes.
- **Delete modal:** the dark background fades and the card grows from 0.96 to full size from its center. It wasn't animating before because a `transition: all` can't run on an element that switches from `display: none`. It also had a 400ms `ease` that didn't match anything else.

**Shared behaviour**
- **Timing:** I used the project's existing tokens. Opening takes `--duration-medium` (250ms), closing takes `--duration-short` (150ms), and both use `--ease-standard`.
- **Showing and hiding:** they now animate both ways (`@starting-style` plus `transition-behavior: allow-discrete`), and each list names only the properties that change. If you reopen something while it's closing, it turns around smoothly instead of jumping. That happens with the toast if you click Save during its fade-out.
- **Reduced motion:** for people who have reduced motion turned on, all three only fade, with no scaling or movement.
- **Older browsers:** browsers from before 2024 don't support this CSS and will show and hide the overlays instantly, as they do now.

**Not changed:** the modal doesn't close on Escape or keep keyboard focus inside it, and the dropdown doesn't close on Escape either. Those are accessibility fixes rather than animation, and I can do them next if you want.

All three now animate open and closed, but I haven't tested this in a browser. The changes are all in `src/styles.css`; `app.js` and `index.html` are unchanged.

**Why the modal wasn't animating:** it switched from `display: none` to `display: flex` and relied on `transition: all 400ms ease`. A browser can't fade from `display: none`, so the modal just appeared. The dropdown and toast had the same problem because the `hidden` attribute also sets `display: none`.

**The fix:** each element now has a starting style to animate from when it opens, and stays on screen until its close animation finishes. Opening takes 300ms and closing takes 150ms, both easing out. Each transition lists only the properties it changes, instead of `all`.

- **Account dropdown:** fades in and grows from 0.96 to full size, starting from its top-right corner (the side nearest the button). Closing reverses this.
- **"Changes saved" toast:** fades in while rising 16px from the bottom of the screen, and drops back down as it fades out.
- **Delete-account modal:** the dark backdrop fades in and the dialog box grows from 0.96 to full size from its centre. Closing reverses this.

If someone has reduced motion turned on in their system settings, all three only fade, with no movement or resizing.

**Browser support:** this relies on CSS features from 2024. Older browsers will still show and hide all three instantly, as they did before, so nothing breaks.

Two things I noticed but didn't change:
- The dropdown's link hover style isn't limited to devices that can hover, so on touchscreens the highlight can stay on after a tap.
- The toast appears and disappears by toggling `hidden` on an element that screen readers watch for announcements. Some screen readers don't announce when it's done that way, so "Changes saved" may not be read aloud.

The empty state now comes in piece by piece instead of all at once. I only changed `src/styles.css`; `index.html` didn't need any changes.

**What it does**
- The four parts appear in order, 100ms apart: the folder icon, "No projects yet", the description, then the two buttons.
- Each part fades in, rises 12px and goes from slightly blurred to sharp over 300ms. The whole thing takes about 0.6s.
- For people who have turned on reduced motion in their system settings, the parts just fade in, still in order, with no movement or blur.
- The hidden starting look exists only inside the animation itself. If the animation doesn't run for any reason, the content still shows normally rather than staying invisible.

**Things to know**
- The animation runs each time the page loads while there are no projects, not only on the very first visit. This page has no script or saved state to tell a first visit from a repeat. Since the empty state goes away once a project exists, that should be fine in practice. If you want it to play only once ever, I can add a small script that remembers it has played.
- The animation applies to every direct child of `.empty-state` in order. If you add or reorder parts, the delays follow their position.
- I haven't checked it in a browser. I worked from the code only, so the timing and the reduced-motion version still need a look on screen.

I added a staggered entrance to the empty state in `src/styles.css`. It's CSS only, and I didn't change the markup in `index.html`.

**What it does:** the empty state's four parts come in one after another, 100ms apart: the folder icon, then "No projects yet", then the description, then the two buttons. Each one fades in, rises 12px and goes from slightly blurred to sharp over 300ms. The whole sequence takes about 0.6s.

**Reduced motion:** if someone has "reduce motion" turned on in their system settings, the parts only fade in, still one after another. There's no movement or blur.

**If the animation fails:** the hidden starting state exists only inside the animation itself. If the animation doesn't run for some reason, the content just shows up normally instead of staying invisible.

**When it plays:** right now the page is static HTML, so the animation runs once each time the page loads. If the empty state is later shown by JavaScript (say, after projects finish loading), it will play when the element is added to the page. It won't replay when other parts of the page update.

I haven't checked this in a browser, so the timing and feel haven't been looked at on screen.
